Peasant Multiplication

ArithmeticAlgorithms
Game: Multiply two numbers using only halving, doubling and adding, the way peasants are said to have done it.
How to play: Press the arrows above a digit to change a number and watch the columns follow. Tick "Show binary" to see why it works.
×

Look for the math

To find a × b, halve a again and again (dropping any remainder) until you reach 1, and double b the same number of times. Then add the doubles that stand beside an odd half. The sum is the product, and nothing more difficult than doubling and adding was needed.

Binary numbers inside

Each time you halve and drop the remainder, the remainder you dropped is the next digit of a written in binary: 1 beside an odd number, 0 beside an even one. For 85 these digits are 1010101, which is 64 + 16 + 4 + 1. So 85 × 18 = 64×18 + 16×18 + 4×18 + 1×18, and those four products are exactly the doubles in the red rows. "Show binary" adds the power of 2 and the digit to every row.

Which number first?

The number of rows is the number of binary digits of the first number. The page advises putting the smaller number first, because it has fewer digits. The test confirmed this for every pair of numbers up to 400, and that the algorithm gives the true product for all 160,000 of them and for 20,000 random four-digit pairs.

Where the name comes from

The method is called Russian peasant or Ethiopian multiplication, and it is close to the doubling in the Egyptian Rhind Papyrus. Computers do the same thing with shifts and adds.

Try 85 × 18 and then 18 × 85. Both give 1530. Which one needs fewer rows?
